name: NEMO
summary: NEMO-3 was a tracking calorimeter at Modane that measured double-beta decay in several isotopes. Separating the isotope foil from the detector allowed reconstruction of both electron tracks, their energies and their opening angle.
detection_principle: Thin source foils are surrounded by gaseous tracking cells and scintillator calorimeters. A magnetic field, time of flight and common-vertex reconstruction identify two-electron events and reject external backgrounds.

results.summary: The final 100Mo analysis found no neutrinoless signal while measuring detailed two-neutrino-decay distributions.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
